source_context_translations.translation: Water is good at benefiting the ten thousand things and does not contend; it dwells in places that others dislike,
therefore it is close to the Way.

Dwelling is best on good ground, the heart is best like a deep pool, association is best in benevolence, speech is best in trustworthiness, government is best in order, affairs are best in ability, and movement is best in season.
Because it does not contend, there is therefore no fault.
Holding and filling it up is not as good as stopping.
Poking and prying into it makes it impossible to preserve for long.
If gold and jade fill the hall, none can keep them safe.
Wealth and rank, if joined with arrogance, bring their own disaster.
When merit is accomplished, the body withdraws; this is the Way of Heaven.
Can you carry your vital spirit and embrace oneness, and so avoid separation?
Can you concentrate your breath and make it gentle, and be like a newborn child?

additional_senses.Dictionary Meaning (English): all people considered together, especially as a broad human collectivity
additional_senses.Nuance (English): Broader and more inclusive than a local or social group.
Sentence Translations (English): Everyone knows his name.
All agreed, and none dared to contend.
When everyone wants to go, I alone do not go.
When everyone saw it, all were astonished.

additional_senses.Dictionary Meaning (English): a crowd or body of people viewed as a group, often with implication of common opinion or behavior
additional_senses.Nuance (English): May emphasize collective conduct or sentiment rather than mere numerical plurality.
Sentence Translations (English): The crowd was in an uproar.
The multitude rushed after gain.
The crowd could not fathom his intention.
All the people followed his command.

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): people at large; the general body of people in contrast to a few or to the noble and high-ranking
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): Often refers to ordinary people collectively, without implying a formal political class.

additional_senses.Dictionary Meaning (English): very nearly, but not quite
additional_senses.Nuance (English): A general proximity sense, often of result or condition.
Sentence Translations (English): It almost failed and then recovered.
He nearly died and then revived.
It was nearly a great achievement.
He was nearly made a laughingstock.

additional_senses.Dictionary Meaning (English): an unspecified small number more than one
additional_senses.Nuance (English): Counts or indicates a small plurality rather than nearness.
Sentence Translations (English): Not seen for several days.
Several people came together.
Several households discussed it together.
Several springs have passed.

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): nearly reaching a state, degree, or standard; on the verge of becoming or being something
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): Marks nearness of degree, not certainty or completion.

additional_senses.Dictionary Meaning (English): marks location or time within which something occurs
additional_senses.Nuance (English): Locative or temporal use with static sense.
Sentence Translations (English): Dwelling in the mountains below.
Born in a troubled age.
Known in the countryside.
Seen today.

additional_senses.Dictionary Meaning (English): introduces the standard in a comparison
additional_senses.Nuance (English): Used after comparatives or words of resemblance.
Sentence Translations (English): Good over evil.
Easy rather than difficult.
Higher than a mountain.
Lighter than a feather.

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): introduces a goal, target, comparison, or relation; indicates direction toward something
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): In this text, marks relation or comparison rather than motion.

additional_senses.Dictionary Meaning (English): a suitable or advantageous location
additional_senses.Nuance (English): Emphasizes fitness of place or situation.
Sentence Translations (English): Choose a good place to dwell.
A good place can give one security.
He dwelled in a good place.
He moved to a good place.

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): a good place to reside or stand; a favorable, secure footing or position
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): Here it praises a stable, suitable place rather than moral goodness alone.

additional_senses.Dictionary Meaning (English): to bestow or grant something to someone
additional_senses.Nuance (English): A direct act of conferral or transfer.
Sentence Translations (English): He gave grain to the people.
He gave him his book.
He shared joy with the people.
He shared it with a friend.

additional_senses.Dictionary Meaning (English): joins words or phrases coordinatively
additional_senses.Nuance (English): A connective use distinct from the prepositional verb.
Sentence Translations (English): Mountains and waters reflect one another.
Heaven and earth unite.
Virtue and power go together.
This differs from that.

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): to interact with or deal with someone in a certain way; to conduct oneself toward another party
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): In this passage it governs the accompanying standard 善仁 and means relational conduct toward others.

additional_senses.Dictionary Meaning (English): the quality of being trustworthy and keeping one's word
additional_senses.Nuance (English): Can refer to the moral state of trustworthiness itself.
Sentence Translations (English): They dealt with one another in good faith.
He lost his trustworthiness.
The gentleman values good faith.
Good faith is practiced in the world.

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): reliable in speech; speaking so that one can trust what is said
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): Describes speech that merits trust, not merely factual correctness.

additional_senses.Dictionary Meaning (English): political administration or public government
additional_senses.Nuance (English): A substantive sense referring to governance as a domain.
Sentence Translations (English): He governed by virtue.
Only after correcting errors was there peace.
The proper ordering of the realm.
Governance is in the court.

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): to administer or manage in a proper and effective way
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): Here it denotes ordered governance, not simply putting things right in a moral sense.

additional_senses.Dictionary Meaning (English): the quality of choosing or meeting the proper moment
additional_senses.Nuance (English): Can name the proper use of opportunity or season.
Sentence Translations (English): Action has its proper time.
Sending out troops values good timing.
Act when the time is right.
Lose the right moment and you fail.

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): suited to the proper time or moment; acting at the right season
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): Highlights appropriateness to circumstances and timing, not mere speed.

additional_senses.Dictionary Meaning (English): to attribute fault or responsibility to someone
additional_senses.Nuance (English): A verbal use focusing on assigning blame.
Sentence Translations (English): People blamed his error.
Do not blame the crowd.
Heaven does not blame people.
The crowd also blamed him.

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): blameworthy error or wrongdoing for which one is responsible
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): Here it means blame attached to conduct, not merely an outward defect.

additional_senses.Dictionary Meaning (English): to hold up or sustain something physically
additional_senses.Nuance (English): Emphasizes bearing weight or sustaining an object.
Sentence Translations (English): He held his staff.
He held it in his hand.
He steadied the boat from capsizing.
He carried a lamp at night.

additional_senses.Dictionary Meaning (English): to keep something in a continuing state
additional_senses.Nuance (English): A sustained, durative sense, often of condition or policy.
Sentence Translations (English): He maintained integrity and did not bend.
It lasted long and remained secure.
He maintained its statutes.
He kept his mind as before.

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): to keep in the hand or maintain in a fixed condition
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): Here it means maintaining possession or position while increasing fullness.

additional_senses.Dictionary Meaning (English): to estimate or gauge by comparing, examining, or probing
additional_senses.Nuance (English): Can denote assessing size, depth, or condition.
Sentence Translations (English): Measure its thickness.
Probe the heart and know it.
Estimate his feelings.
Gauge the situation.

additional_senses.Dictionary Meaning (English): to infer or guess inwardly, often without certainty
additional_senses.Nuance (English): A mental guessing sense, weaker and more tentative than knowledge.
Sentence Translations (English): I suspect his intention.
People suspect his guilt.
The crowd guessed and doubted him.
The gentleman does not make mere guesses.

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): to poke, probe, or test by pressing and measuring out the inner condition of something
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): A testing, probing action that can expose what should remain intact.

additional_senses.Dictionary Meaning (English): something that supports or braces another thing
additional_senses.Nuance (English): A concrete support or brace.
Sentence Translations (English): Without a prop, it leans over.
Use a prop to support the roof.
Wood served as its brace.
Remove the support and it falls.

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): to prop up, uphold, or raise by means of a support
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): Here it suggests forcing something up or propping it out so it loses natural integrity.

additional_senses.Dictionary Meaning (English): to ensure that something remains safe or certain
additional_senses.Nuance (English): Can mean to secure a result or person against harm or loss.
Sentence Translations (English): Who can guarantee it?
Ensure that it remains free from harm.
The gentleman protects the people.
He preserved his body intact.

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): to keep safe from loss, damage, or change over time
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): A durative sense of keeping something intact and secure.

additional_senses.Dictionary Meaning (English): valuable objects or wealth regarded collectively
additional_senses.Nuance (English): Can stand broadly for costly possessions.
Sentence Translations (English): He amassed treasure in his house.
Gold and jade are not long kept.
People covet treasure.
Gold and jade can mislead people.

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): precious metals and gemstones; valuables of great worth
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): A standard paired expression for valuables and treasure.

additional_senses.Dictionary Meaning (English): to make or become full
additional_senses.Nuance (English): Verbal use of filling or becoming full.
Sentence Translations (English): When a vessel is full, it overflows.
The water filled the river.
Virtue filled his person.
Full, yet not arrogant.

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): filled to capacity; having no empty space left
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): Describes complete filling, often with an implication that excess is unstable.

additional_senses.Dictionary Meaning (English): the central or principal part of a building or estate
additional_senses.Nuance (English): Sometimes more specifically the main household court or principal chamber.
Sentence Translations (English): He entered the hall.
There were guests in the hall.
He ascended the hall to meet them.
Vessels were arranged before the hall.

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): a large reception room or main chamber in a house or building
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): A principal indoor space, often of a residence or official building.

additional_senses.Dictionary Meaning (English): to lack or not possess
additional_senses.Nuance (English): A broader negation of possession or presence.
Sentence Translations (English): There is no benefit to be had.
One has no way in.
No one knows the cause.
Under heaven none does not hear it.

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): there is no one or nothing to; no person or thing exists to perform the action
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): An existential negator meaning absence of anyone capable or available.

additional_senses.Dictionary Meaning (English): possessing wealth and elevated status
additional_senses.Nuance (English): Can describe persons, families, or circumstances.
Sentence Translations (English): His household was rich and noble.
Rich and noble, he became arrogant.
Wealth and rank are not constant by Heaven.
He did not seek wealth and rank.

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): material affluence and high social standing or official position
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): A conventional pairing for prosperity plus status, often morally fraught in the text.

additional_senses.Dictionary Meaning (English): to have pride or self-exaltation
additional_senses.Nuance (English): A broader state of pride, not always overtly offensive.
Sentence Translations (English): Pride does not last long.
When people are proud, they fail.
The gentleman is not proud.
Few who are rich are proud.

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): showing overbearing pride and treating others as beneath oneself
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): Implies pride that leads to overreach and social or moral harm.

additional_senses.Dictionary Meaning (English): to leave or bequeath something behind
additional_senses.Nuance (English): A concrete transfer or remainder sense, often with an object left behind.
Sentence Translations (English): He left a letter behind.
He left people behind in the wilderness.
He left him wealth.
He left not a single thing behind.

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): to cause a fault, loss, or harm to fall on oneself by one's own action
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): Here it means self-inflicted acquisition of misfortune or blame.

additional_senses.Dictionary Meaning (English): misfortune or disaster
additional_senses.Nuance (English): Can denote a harmful outcome rather than personal blame.
Sentence Translations (English): The calamity came upon his own person.
Virtue spared him from disaster.
He brought the fault on himself.
He left to avoid calamity.

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): a blameworthy error, offense, or misdeed that brings reproach or harm
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): A serious failing with moral or practical consequence.

additional_senses.Dictionary Meaning (English): thereupon; afterwards; as a consequence
additional_senses.Nuance (English): A sequential-result adverb.
Sentence Translations (English): He then carried out his intention.
The army arrived and then withdrew.
When matters were settled, he then returned.
Upon hearing the order, he left at once.

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): to bring a task, work, or aim to completion
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): Focuses on completion or success of an undertaking.

additional_senses.Dictionary Meaning (English): to reduce, fall back, or lessen in status or strength
additional_senses.Nuance (English): Can refer to waning, receding, or dropping away.
Sentence Translations (English): The momentum gradually declined.
The illness eased somewhat.
The tide receded and the sand appeared.
When the qi retreats, cold follows.

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): to move back, retire, or step away from a position or undertaking
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): In this passage it implies retiring after success, not simple retreat in battle only.

additional_senses.Dictionary Meaning (English): to put cargo or a burden on something
additional_senses.Nuance (English): Can mean placing something on a vehicle, beast, or person as a load.
Sentence Translations (English): Load it onto the cart.
The boat can carry people.
He carried grain back.
The cart was loaded with things.

additional_senses.Dictionary Meaning (English): a coordinating conjunction in some classical styles, especially in fixed or rhythmic parallelism
additional_senses.Nuance (English): Rare in this simple form; mainly relevant where syntactic coordination is intended.
Sentence Translations (English): They went and they stopped.
They sang and they danced.
They galloped and they rushed.
They laughed and they spoke.

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): to bear, wear, or place above oneself as if on the head; to support or uphold
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): Here it conveys bearing and sustaining, not simply transporting.

additional_senses.Dictionary Meaning (English): the animating soul-like and corporeal spirit-like components of a person
additional_senses.Nuance (English): Can point to the two complementary spirit-aspects in human life.
Sentence Translations (English): When the spirit is calm, the body is at peace.
When spirit leaves, illness follows.
He concentrated on guarding his spirit.
He nourished his vital spirit.

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): the animate, vital aspect of a person conceived as a psychophysical presence
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): A dual-vitality term from early Chinese thought, referring to the enlivened self rather than a technical later psychology.

additional_senses.Dictionary Meaning (English): to clasp or keep in one's arms or hands
additional_senses.Nuance (English): Physical holding, often close and secure.
Sentence Translations (English): He carried the child in his arms.
He held it with his hands.
He sat holding a book.
He clutched the wood and would not let go.

additional_senses.Dictionary Meaning (English): to keep something in the heart with attachment or care
additional_senses.Nuance (English): A mental or emotional holding sense, often of plans or beliefs.
Sentence Translations (English): He cherished his resolve and did not change.
He harbored resentment in his heart.
He acted while cherishing benevolence.
He kept to his old promise.

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): to hold close to oneself or keep together
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): Here it is figurative: holding fast to oneness and not letting it scatter.

additional_senses.Dictionary Meaning (English): the numeral or the single unit itself
additional_senses.Nuance (English): The ordinary counting sense.
Sentence Translations (English): Only one person.
One day covers a thousand miles.
They unite into one body.
Its Way returns to one.

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): the condition of being one, unified, or undivided
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): In this passage it denotes undivided inward unity rather than the numeral alone.

additional_senses.Dictionary Meaning (English): to leave a place or person
additional_senses.Nuance (English): A plain motion-away sense.
Sentence Translations (English): He left home and traveled on.
It is several li from here.
He rose and left the mat.
He has been away from home a long time.

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): to part from, leave, or become divided from something previously joined
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): In this passage it means falling apart from the one-ness being held.

additional_senses.Dictionary Meaning (English): devoted to one thing only; not divided among several things
additional_senses.Nuance (English): Describes focused singleness of purpose.
Sentence Translations (English): He concentrated on learning the Way.
He held a single resolve without division.
He devoted himself to his post.
He was single-minded and unmixed.

additional_senses.Dictionary Meaning (English): to keep something to oneself or control it alone
additional_senses.Nuance (English): An uncommon but established social sense in later classical prose.
Sentence Translations (English): He monopolized the profit for himself.
He monopolized power and used it at will.
He kept it to himself and shared it with no one.
He monopolized the advantage and deprived the many.

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): to make single-minded or undivided, especially by gathering and fixing attention or vital force
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): Here it means to gather inwardly and eliminate dispersion.

additional_senses.Dictionary Meaning (English): the atmosphere or air around us
additional_senses.Nuance (English): Concrete physical air, wind, or vapor.
Sentence Translations (English): The air in the mountains is cold.
Air entered the room.
When the air stirs, wind rises.
The vapor rises and clouds form.

additional_senses.Dictionary Meaning (English): a person's inner disposition, mood, or moral-spiritual bearing
additional_senses.Nuance (English): Can denote a settled inner condition or character, not just breath or gas.
Sentence Translations (English): When the temper is harmonious, speech is smooth.
His temperament was very firm.
Nourish the vital force to set the heart right.
Observe a person's bearing and know him.

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): the breath or inner vital force that animates living beings
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): In this passage it refers to vital breath as something to be made gentle and unified.
